steps.title: In the ground

form.name: Ytterbium in ion-adsorption clay
form.label: 2 to 3% of the rare earths in clays

steps.text: The seventeen rare earths always occur together, never alone. The heavy ones, ytterbium among them, are scarce in the hard-rock ores. Their main source is ion-adsorption clay in southern China and Myanmar, where they cling loosely to weathered granite. Xenotime is another source.

steps.title: Mine
steps.text: No digging is needed for the clays. A salt solution, usually ammonium sulphate, is pumped into the hillside; it washes the rare earths off the clay and drains out at the bottom, where they are precipitated as a mixed carbonate. The method is cheap and can foul soil and water.
steps.india: 2,900 tonnes of rare-earth oxide in 2025, 0.7% of the world, all from monazite in beach sands worked by IREL.

steps.title: Dissolve
steps.text: The mixed carbonate from the clays is dissolved in hydrochloric acid and filtered. There is no hard mineral to break down, and little of the thorium that comes with monazite. What is left is a mixed rare-earth chloride: all the elements still together.

steps.title: Separate
steps.text: This is the hard part. Neighbouring rare earths behave almost identically, so the solution is run through hundreds of solvent-extraction stages, each shifting the balance slightly, until ytterbium comes out on its own as an oxide. China does about 91% of the world's separation.

steps.title: Make
steps.text: Ytterbium oxide is doped into the core of laser fibre. For medicine it is enriched in the isotope ytterbium-176 and pressed into reactor targets.
steps.india: CSIR-CGCRI makes ytterbium-doped double-clad fibre for high-power lasers.

steps.title: Use
steps.text: Ytterbium-doped fibre lasers cut and weld metal in factories and are the basis of most high-power industrial lasers. Enriched ytterbium is the starting material for lutetium-177 cancer therapy, and ytterbium atoms keep time in the most accurate clocks.
steps.india: BARC's lutetium-177 route uses ytterbium targets. IREL seeks 2.5 tonnes of ytterbium oxide.

steps.title: Recycle
steps.text: Very little is recovered from old products: each one holds grams, spread thin and hard to collect. Scrap from the factories that make these materials is the main source.
